question.text: Identify the Incan ruler whom Pizarro seized and executed after demanding and receiving a roomful of gold as ransom.
question.clue: He offered to fill a large room with gold and silver for his ransom, but the Spaniards didn't release him.

swap.text: The Incan empire was centered in this modern day country, whose capital is Lima.
swap.clue: This country's native leader Tupac Amaru rebelled in 1780 and Jose de San Martin became its Protector in 1821.

question.text: Alongside Bernardo O'Higgins, de San Martin fought for the independence of this future nation. The Battle of Junin was part of this country's war of independence.
question.clue: The second half of A Fish in the Water is a memoir by a candidate for this country's presidency, whose FREDEMO coalition lost to a man supported by APRA and Cambio 90.

swap.leadin: Name some things about pre-Columbian Peru.
swap.text: This southern Peruvian civilization created an aqueduct system that still works. It drew lines in spider, fish, and lizard shapes in a namesake desert, and also shares its name with a tectonic plate that borders the Andes.
swap.clue: This culture built the Cantalloc ("cahn-TAH-yoke")Aqueducts, exemplifying the corkscrew entrances of their puquios ("poo-KEE-ohʼs").

question.text: This conquistador kidnapped and executed Atahualpa before proceeding to crush the Inca Empire. He later founded Lima, the capital of modern-day Peru.

swap.leadin: In its native Quechua tongue it is known as Tawantinsuyu or "Land of the Four Quarters"
swap.text: Identify this empire conquered by the Spanish and whose mita system was used by the Spanish to run the silver mines at Potosi.
swap.clue: A civil war in this empire was won by a son born outside its royal family, and who allegedly ordered the execution of his brother.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the House of Garcilaso de la Vega.
question.text: The chronicler Garcilaso de la Vega wrote La Florida and The Royal Commentaries of [this group], becoming the first New World author to be read in Europe. He was nicknamed "El [this ethnic group]."
question.clue: The language Quechua was spoken by members of this empire.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain precious metal in pre-Columbian South America.
swap.text: Tales of gold in South America inspired legends of this fictitious "City of Gold." This fictional place was sought by Europeans like Walter Raleigh and Gonzalo de Quesada.
swap.answerHtml: El Dorado [accept Manoa; do NOT accept or prompt on “Cibola”]
swap.clue: During the first part of the journey in which Orellana travelled the length of the Amazon, a valley of Cinnamon and this place were the targets of Gonzalo Pizzaro.

question.leadin: Jim Woodmann constructed a balloon using primitive materials in order to show the plausibility of the "balloon theory" regarding these things.
question.text: Identify these archaeological features which include the Condor and the Hummingbird. Jainer Jesus Flores Vigo was arrested for using a truck as an "attack against cultural heritage" on these things in 2018.
question.answerHtml: Nazca Lines [or Nasca Lines; or Andes Lines; or Nazca Drawings]
question.clue: These things were damaged by Greenpeace activists wearing improper footwear as part of a 2014 protest.

swap.leadin: A socialist leader with mixed descent from these people, Juan Jose Torres, was overthrown in a US backed coup d'etat led by Hugo Banzer.
swap.text: Name these people whose flag is known as the Wiphala. A leader of the cocalero movement descended from these people founded the pro-indigenous MAS party.
swap.clue: The katarismo movement which has sought to empower this group since the 1970s is named for the husband of martyr Bartolina Sisa.

question.leadin: The Aschers did work uncoding the number system used on these devices, where zero is represented by a missing knot.
question.text: Name these devices. Made from knotted string, these devices were extensively used in the administration of the Inca prior to their invasion by Francisco Pizarro.
question.clue: This objects that were used for record-keeping and other purposes by the Inca.

swap.leadin: One hypothesis suggests that this culture may have created early hot air balloons to view certain artistic features.
swap.text: Name this Peruvian culture that succeeded the Paracas culture. These people carved stone geoglyphs, such as monkeys and spiders, into the desert in their namesake "lines."
swap.clue: Paul Kosok and Maria Reiche (RAI-keh) mapped structures created by these people.

question.text: Kidnapped Chinese workers were also kept in slave-like conditions on these Peruvian islands in order to harvest guano. Spain seized these islands in 1864, which prompted a war in which Chile and Peru fought to take them back.
question.clue: Peruvian magnates on these islands hired blackbirders to kidnap workers to mine guano. Spain seized these islands to acquire those mines in the 1860s, but was repulsed by a coalition of South American countries.

swap.leadin: Construction with this quality, visible at the Acllahuasi at Cuzco, necessitated masons to precisely shape stones to fit with other pieces on site.
swap.text: Name or describe this limitation of the rubble masonry in Incan walls. The term "drystone" refers to masonry made with this limitation.
swap.answerHtml: built without mortar [accept answer involving no fill or material between stones]

question.text: This Incan ruler lost a civil war to his half-brother Atahualpa, after their father Huayna Capac's death from smallpox led to a succession crisis.
question.clue: After the death of his father Huayna Capac, Atahualpa fought this brother for control of the Inca Empire. He was defeated and imprisoned after losses at Chimborazo and Quipaipan.

swap.leadin: This city was the location of a "Ransom Room" full of gold offered by a ruler to his captor.
swap.text: Name this city. A battle named for this city allegedly began after that aforementioned ruler threw down a Bible presented to him by Vincente de Valverde.
swap.answerHtml: Cajamarca (“ka-ha-MAR-ka”) [or Kashamarka; accept Battle of Cajamarca; accept Massacre at Cajamarca]
swap.clue: The mixed-race Juan Garcia held a post as town crier in this Peruvian city after participating in Pizarro's conquest of the Inca Empire, during which Atahualpa was captured in this city led by a lord who collaborated with the Spanish.

question.text: Lying at the confluence of the Huatanay and Tullmayo rivers, it was purportedly founded by Manco Capac. Among its tourist attractions is the church of La Merced.
question.clue: This city whose Quechua name means "center."

swap.leadin: The artwork of this culture shows a spider god called the "Decapitator" holding a knife and a severed head, an indication that these people practiced human sacrifice.
swap.text: Name this civilization whose adobe temple at Huaca del Sol near Cerro Blanco is considered by many to be the largest pre-Columbian structure in South America.

question.leadin: This civilization had its capital at Chanchan, to the north of Trujillo, and its language of Quingnam has been called the "Fisherman's language."
question.text: Name this South American civilization that arose around 900 AD, and was known for its pottery and metallurgy.
question.clue: These people succeeded the Moche, and they ruled from their capital at Chan Chan.

swap.text: Original language term required. Shamans at Chavin de Huantar also used the shells of Strombus galeatus as these musical instruments. Incan messengers known as ch'aski later used these conches to signal their arrival.
